inputs.modified_text:
Just heard about this ruling from the Punjab and Haryana High Court with Justice Sumeet Goel. It states that anticipatory bail can't be yanked simply because stolen articles weren't recovered or the accusations seem serious. There has to be actual evidence of someone abusing their freedom or a new development before any cancellation, and they rejected the attempt to cancel the pre-arrest bail in this house case.

This stands out as a pushback against a justice system built on unproven claims and scare tactics to strip basic freedoms from the most vulnerable among us. It lays bare how these loose standards entrench inequality, letting institutions target working people and marginalized communities with almost no accountability. We need urgent, deeper reforms to protect rights and dismantle the structural discrimination that keeps these oppressive patterns alive.
